news.title: Training Report: Bayern Munich injured stars almost ready; World Cup contingent out a little longer; and MORE!
news.lede: It has been a busy few days for Bayern Munich when it comes to personnel news. News that emerged on Sunday from Säbener Straße indicated that Bayern Munich stars Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala could be back in team training this week (per Bild via @iMiaSanMia): > Among the players currently recovering from injury, Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala are the most advanced in their rehab. Both are expected back in team training at the beginning of the coming week [@BILD] In addition, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia) is reporting that Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano are getting more time off and will not be fully back in action until next week: > Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano have been given more vacation time and won’t return to Munich until the end of the coming week.

news.title: Football associations call for 'leadership that serves football' in fresh Infantino criticism
news.lede: FOOTBALL ASSOCIATIONS UEFA, Concacaf and AFC have called for accountability and unity in a new open letter criticising Fifa president Gianni Infantino. The European, Asian and North, Central America and Caribbean Association published a strongly-worded open letter this morning accusing Infantino of “abandoning” duty and saying he has placed himself “above the collective that entrusted him with authority”. It follows threats of a boycott by these associations after the Infantino launched a plan to bring private investment into Fifa competitions, including the World Cup. The plan was withdrawn within days after Uefa, Concacaf, AFC and a host of others in the world of football strongly condemned it.

news.title: Soccer leaders in Europe, North America, Asia accuse FIFA of ‘deception' over World Cup plans
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino abandoned his proposal to sell commercial rights to the World Cup, but the controversy didn’t end there. Here’s why the proposal sparked global backlash and what it could mean for the FIFA president’s future. UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC believe that FIFA president Gianni Infantino's recent plans to sell an interest in the World Cup was a “fundamental breach of trust” with the institutions world soccer's governing body serves. In an “open letter to the football family” revealed on Monday, UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC also said that “when trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

news.title: World Cup host cities ask Infantino for promised millions, Fifa remains silent
news.lede: The host cities are Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Dallas, Houston, Kansas City, Atlanta, Philadelphia, New York/New Jersey, Miami and Boston. The American host cities for the 2026 World Cup are demanding millions of dollars from FIFA, which they claim the world football governing body promised them, but the money has not yet been paid, writes Atletik. Ahead of the 2025 Club World Cup in the United States, FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced that each of the 11 host cities would receive $1 million as a “legacy” from the tournament. The money was to be used to build small-scale soccer fields and support community projects.

news.title: Ryan Giggs urged 'outstanding' England World Cup star to join Man Utd
news.lede: Manchester United legend Ryan Giggs (Picture: Getty) Ryan Giggs ‘tried to persuade’ England World Cup star Elliot Anderson to join Manchester United before his £116m move to Manchester City. Anderson signed a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium last month after Man City briefly made him the most expensive British player in history. Manchester United were interested in beating their local rivals to a deal but pulled out of the race once Nottingham Forest’s demands went above £100m. Anderson became arguably Forest’s most important player following his £35m move from Newcastle United, helping the club finish seventh in the Premier League and qualify for Europe.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: UEFA signs joint letter slamming 'deception' at top of FIFA as World Cup stake sale fallout continues
news.lede: UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC have hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Gianni Infantino's botched World Cup stake sale plans to further raise the pressure on the under-fire FIFA president. The three continental associations each signed a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception". In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

news.title: UEFA and Allies Attack Infantino: "Football Isn't His, Trust Betrayed by Deceit"
news.lede: Another broadside has been fired at Gianni Infantino, but more significantly, the first real considerations for alternative competitions are emerging. The FIFA president's idea to privatise the World Cup has been met with widespread disapproval. As a result, UEFA, Concacaf, and AFC – the confederations for Europe, North America, and Asia – have issued a joint statement against the FIFA chief. The statement was signed by Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA President; Salman Bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, AFC President; and Victor Montagliani, Concacaf President, along with the general secretaries of all three confederations.

news.title: FIFA Leadership Accused of Breach of Trust over World Cup Rights Plan
news.lede: TEHRAN (Tasnim) – UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF on Monday accused FIFA leadership of a “fundamental breach of trust” over its handling of a proposal to sell a stake in World Cup commercial rights, calling for greater accountability and an independent review.
